Use the worst case, not the headline number. With 54 checks behind it, that is what the record actually supports — the higher figure is the luckiest reading of the same data. Few checks means a low worst case even when the headline looks good. That is the honest answer, not a broken one.

What we are actually measuring

A guess at where a crypto pair goes over the next hour, from fifteen-minute price and volume patterns. The count is how often the direction was right.

What this will not tell you

  • Not whether the move was large enough to cover fees and spread. Most fifteen-minute moves are not, which is why most forecasts here are recorded rather than called.
  • Not how big the move will be. We count which way it went, not how far.
  • Not whether it still works today. Patterns fade once people spot them.

What to do about it

Risk per position
0.00%

Even taking the worst case, this is no better than a coin flip. Risk nothing until that changes.

This is deliberately small: a quarter of the largest bet the maths allows, worked out from the worst case rather than the headline number, and never above 2% of your money. Sizing off the headline is how accounts get wiped out while the idea itself was still fine.

Paper portfolio 8,665 round trips

Being right and making money are different questions. This replays every scored prediction as a position, charges real costs both ways, and reports what the signals would actually have paid. No broker is connected and no order was placed.

-45.36%

Following every signal would have LOST 45.36% over 8,665 round trips. Costs alone took 19,800. Worst peak-to-trough fall along the way: 48.4%.

The replay follows models that have not cleared their skill gate. Finding out whether they are worth money is exactly what it is for, and the answer is allowed to be no.

Every call that went wrong, and by how much. A good idea is still wrong roughly a third of the time — what matters is whether one reason keeps repeating.

Why it went wrong

What we do about it

A single miss means nothing — an idea that is right two times in three is wrong the other time, and reacting to each one is chasing noise. This one repeated 8 times, which is the part worth reading. That is the whole reason for sorting misses by cause.
